messages:
olivia: @channel noticing a spike in SSE disconnect reports from APAC users starting ~2026-03-15 03:00 UTC. Customers report partial streams, reconnect loops, and 403s on subsequent reconnects. ticket IDs: #C-9821, #C-9834.

mike: any error patterns in the ingress logs?

raj: looking now. early sign: proxy is returning 502 for keepalive handshake to the fanout service, then the client SDK retries, we get TOCs in the log.

olivia: copying a snippet from customer logs:

olivia: ```
client: connected
client: received chunk "data: {\"text\": \"Hello\"}\n"
client: connection closed unexpectedly, status 0
client: reconnecting...
```

sarah: internal logs show heartbeat TTL expiring in the fanout pool around 03:02 UTC. Heartbeat monitor shows gaps of ~12s vs expected 3s.

mike: which region/edge? ap-southeast-1?

raj: yes APAC edge nodes. I see elevated CPU on the fanout workers + a burst of ephemeral connections from a single customer IP range. Might be a malformed keepalive rate from a client causing exhaustion.

olivia: we also saw a secondary symptom: some reconnect attempts fail with `401` when token rotation happens immediately after disconnect. Customers see reconnect loop then auth failures.

support-bot: elevated SSE disconnects detected: 03:00-03:15 UTC, apac-edge. Alert ID: SSE-APAC-2026-03-15-01

mike: repro plan — create a small loadtest that opens many long-lived SSE connections and simulates heartbeat jitter. raj, can you script?

raj: yes. I'll run a 500-conn test from our test harness against apac-edge with heartbeat jitter up to 15s. Will also toggle token rotation to repro 401 behavior.

oncall: is there an easy mitigation for customers? Can we flip to fallback polling or a different endpoint?

olivia: we can failover to the regional fallback domain (apac-fallback.redwood-inference.com) which uses a different fanout pool without multiplexing. We should also temporarily relax per-conn ephemeral limits.

ops-lead: I'll prepare a config rollback to disable HTTP/2 connection multiplexing on the apac edge for 15m as a mitigation. That will force one SSE per upstream connection.

mike: please validate impact on costs/throughput — multiplexing helps but preventing disconnect storms is higher priority.

raj: test run results: with jitter up to 15s, the multiplexed pool shows heartbeat TTL misses and connection resets at 20% of streams. The non-multiplexed fallback pool shows <1% resets. Also reproduced token-rotation 401 when reconnect happened within 5s of token refresh.

olivia: customer workaround: set SDK option `maxReconnectAttempts` to 6 and enable `usePollingIfReconnectFails=true`. Documented repro steps:

olivia: ```
// JS SDK example
const stream = new Redwood.SSEStream({
  url: 'https://api.redwood.com/stream',
  heartbeatIntervalMs: 3000,
  maxReconnectAttempts: 6,
  fallbackToPolling: true
});
```

mike: ops-lead, ready to push the disable-multiplexing patch?

ops-lead: preparing now. Will route through deploy-bot for canary to two apac nodes.

deploy-bot: queued deploy: disable-multiplexing-apac v1.2.3 -> canary nodes (2/10)

raj: after canary, fanout CPU dropped 35%, heartbeat TTLs back to normal, disconnect rate dropped from ~18% to 0.8% in canary.

olivia: can we also patch the token refresh window handling? There is a race where reconnect uses old token, server rejects with 401 while the client attempts immediate retry with renewed token but we return 429 on the second attempt because of retry throttling.

mike: create a short-term patch: allow a 5s grace period after token rotation where reconnect attempts are allowed without counting against retry throttle. Then upstream can do proper fix in SDK and token service.

raj: implemented grace rule on auth gateway. Testing now.

support-bot: status page update suggested: "Partial SSE degradation in APAC affecting streaming stability. Mitigation in progress: routing affected customers to fallback pool. No data loss reported."

olivia: I've drafted an incident post for status.redwood.com with steps customers can take and the temporary SDK settings. Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-apac-sse

mike: after the canary looked good, ops-lead rolled out to remaining apac nodes at 03:40 UTC. Disconnects dropped to baseline.

ops-lead: full rollback window set to 24h; keep multiplexing disabled until further notice. We'll monitor CPU and reconnects.

raj: follow-up actions
- add rate-limiting on malformed keepalives per upstream IP
- update SDK to jitter reconnects + backoff, and honor token refresh grace
- add a synthetic that simulates token rotation mid-stream in load tests

olivia: customer comms: sent notes to affected customers offering one-on-one support and extended request quota for 24h while we stabilize.

oncall: any immediate alerts to suppress? we should keep the alert for now but reduce noise by combining similar tokens into one alert thread.

mike: adding an eval job to check model fallback behavior in case of streaming drop for customers relying on streaming completions. We need to verify fallback to non-streaming still returns full outputs and billing is correct.

olivia: billing note: some customers saw duplicate billable connect attempts; finance will reconcile duplicates for the affected window. I've opened FIN ticket #FIN-2404.

support-bot: incident resolved: mitigation applied 03:40 UTC, monitoring shows stable connections. Ticket escalations: #C-9821, #C-9834 moved to support queue for follow-up.

olivia: thanks everyone. We'll keep multiplexing disabled in APAC for at least 24h and push SDK improvements next sprint. I'll send a postmortem draft by EOD."
